title: CUPID in the Model Zoo: Online Matchmaking for Selecting Your Dream LLM
claim: By inferring hidden user preferences against hidden model capabilities, our method navigates the space directly and accumulates less regret than baselines.
layout: Top schematic banner above two plot panels; left-to-right; shaded efficiency-gain region
description: The figure has a top banner and two plots below it. The banner shows a beige cloud, "Latent User Objectives" (tone, personality, verbosity, style, correctness, with a question mark). An arrow leads from it into a central blue rounded box. A grey cloud, "Latent LLM Capabilities" (reasoning, creativity, intelligence, fluency), sends an arrow into the same box from the right. Inside the box, "HEART-UCB" and a "BEST Match" badge are joined by yellow cyclic arrows labeled "Iterative Latent Belief Updating" and "User Feedback". The bottom left panel is a 2-D scatter of model candidates. A green CUPID path runs straight to a gold star marking the user's latent preference. A red dashed standard-bandit path wanders. A callout reads "Too formal, be brief!". The bottom right panel plots cumulative regret against interaction rounds. Random selection (dotted grey) and the standard bandit (dashed red) both sit above the green CUPID curve, and the gap between them is shaded green as the efficiency gain.
caption: To help users with latent objectives to find matching LLMs with matching capabilities, CUPID efficiently navigates a latent preference space. This targeted navigation results in lower cumulative regret, allowing the system to quickly identify the optimal model at a lower cost.
abstract: Users increasingly face the challenge of selecting an appropriate LLM for a given task from a rapidly growing pool of LLMs, each with distinct but often opaque latent properties. Compounding this challenge, users may lack the vocabulary or awareness to explicitly articulate the characteristics they value in an LLM's responses or deployment. We propose an interaction-efficient active learning framework in which a dueling bandit algorithm iteratively selects pairs of LLMs, collects user feedback about their responses, and updates its belief about the user's latent preferences. We introduce a novel belief-aware upper confidence bound strategy that balances exploration of the model pool with exploitation of inferred preferences, enabling efficient alignment between user needs and LLM capabilities under user-specified cost and time budgets. Through diverse experiments on LLMs and human studies, we experimentally verify that our model can efficiently match well-aligned LLMs to users at a lower cost.
